Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Household, washing & chores

dump verb

throw down or away

also throw away, throw down, chuck, discard

classical

Gell. 15.17.1: abjēcit īnfrēgitque
Mor. 96: spargit humī atque abjicit

abjiciō, abjicere, abjēcī, abjectum

verb, third conjugation

throw down, throw away

Of throwing something down or away as unwanted; humī abjicere, to dump on the ground or the floor. Tipping a load out is effundō (pour out).

Examples

  • et summīs spoliat coriīs contemptaque passim spargit humī atque abjicit

    and he strips off the outer skins and scatters the unwanted bits about on the floor and throws them awayMor. 95–96

  • trāditās sibi tībiās, cum ad ōs adhibuisset īnflāssetque, pudēfactus ōris dēfōrmitāte abjēcit īnfrēgitque

    when he had been handed the pipes and had put them to his lips and blown, he was so ashamed of how they spoiled his face that he threw them down and broke themGell. 15.17.1

  • prō sē quisque, quod cēperat, adferēbat, ante pedēs Pȳthiī piscēs abjiciēbantur

    each man brought what he had caught, and the fish were dumped at Pythius’ feetCic. Off. 3.58

See also pour out, rubbish, rubbish bin, throw, dump truck.
